newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Disney throws a fifth anniversary party.
newsitem.headline: Euro Disney throws a fifth anniversary party.

text.p: Euro Disney's Paris theme park, decried at birth by French intellectuals as a "cultural Chernobyl", celebrates its fifth anniversary on Saturday as Europe's biggest tourist attraction.
Disneyland Paris drew nearly 12 million people last year, twice as many as the Eiffel Tower and five times as many as the Tower of London.

"With more than 50 million visitors since the opening, we've proved our ability to attract a huge flow of tourists," new chairman Gilles Pelisson told the annual general meeting in March. "Europe has definitely adopted Disneyland Paris."
Even in France, where the Disney brand of entertainment was dismissed as too bland and too American, one in five inhabitants has been to the park at least once, said a company spokesman.
Last November, despite cautious consumer spending that has hit France's leisure industry, Euro Disney reported a second consecutive profit for its October-to-September fiscal year.
But investors in the company feel bewildered after a five-year rollercoaster ride that has left the stock at a fraction of its offer price.
It was trading at 10.00 francs on Thursday, down 85 percent from an all-time high four years ago before Euro Disney's 20 billion franc debt burden nearly drove it into the ground.

The company was saved by a financial restructuring which included a holiday on debt payments and royalty and management fees to The Walt Disney Co., which owns 39 percent. But as the holiday comes to a close, the repayment schedule entails a steep rise in the company's financial costs.

"Only the appointment of Cinderella's fairy godmother herself, complete with magic wand, could solve Euro Disney's main problem, which is still its financial debt burden," Morgan Stanley analyst Rebecca Winnington-Ingram wrote in a report.

"Any further improvements at the operating profit line, which has been steadily increasing for the past three years, will likely be gobbled up by increasing financing charges as the benefits of the debt moratorium negotiated in 1994 are gradually phased out," she wrote.
"Euro Disney's a huge commercial success and its survival is no longer at risk, but what's missing is profit growth," said financial analyst Antoine Nodet at brokerage Dupont Denant.
"Their financial costs are climbing, and they can't raise prices because of the depressed economic climate," he said.

Company officials say the commercial success of the theme park, packed with more than 40 attractions including the Space Mountain thrill ride, will lead to financial rewards when the economy picks up and visitors start to spend more freely.
A spokesman said nearly a third of the visitors to the theme park in Marne-la-Vallee east of the French capital have come at least once before.
Adjacent developments, which will not be financed by Euro Disney but by third parties, are expected to generate more business.

An eight-screen Gaumont cinema is scheduled to open at the end of April, a second convention centre is under construction and should open in the autumn, and public authorities have approved the development of a commercial shopping centre.
